description: Sundowner is a team drawn to a problem that will grow as humans travel farther from Earth: crews will have to protect their own health, often with little time and no doctor nearby. Our work starts from that moment of decision. We named the team after the time of day when the light changes, because that is when many people begin to look for safety. We are looking for teammates who can help with coding and finding data.
summary: Sundowner is an interactive website that explores how a journey to Mars could affect an astronaut’s body. Visitors can examine body systems through a 3D model, try simulated mission decisions, and see how their effects might add up over time. NASA research informs the explanations; crew readings and outcomes are simulated for learning.
details: We built Sundowner to make astronaut health easier to understand. Visitors can explore radiation, bones and muscles, sleep, cardiovascular health, and immunity. They can also test scenarios such as a spacewalk or a missed workout and see how those choices might affect a mission. The site works on desktop and mobile. Its health scores are illustrative, not real medical readings or diagnoses.
